predecessors.name: Habsburg monarchy
predecessors.text: the border zone of the Kingdoms of Croatia and Slavonia, where Ferdinand I "began building the defense system" after the Habsburgs were elected kings of Croatia in 1526

successors.name: Kingdom of Croatia Slavonia
successors.text: the Croatian and Slavonian frontiers, "abolished and incorporated into the Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia" by the decree of 15 July 1881 and the takeover of 1 August

successors.name: Austria-Hungary
successors.text: the Banat Frontier, "abolished on 8 August [1873] and incorporated into Hungary"

ledger.x: 1553: the Habsburgs establish the Military Frontier against the Ottomans.
1699: "The Treaty of Karlowitz returned former Ottoman lands, which were largely absorbed into the frontier."

26 January 1699 (Karlowitz): the Military Frontier page says it "expanded onto former Ottoman territories in Lika, Kordun, Banija, lower Slavonia, Syrmia" after the Great Turkish War; it gives no date for lower Slavonia and Syrmia within 1699-1702.
1702: the river sections are formed on the lands Karlowitz returned: "Danube, Tisa, Mureș, and Sava sections existed (1702 to 1751)".
1718: the Peace of Passarowitz brings northern Bosnia into the Frontier.
1739: northern Bosnia leaves the Frontier ("From 1718 to 1739"); the page names no treaty.
1745: northern Slavonia becomes the civil Kingdom of Slavonia; southern Slavonia and Syrmia stay the Slavonian Military Frontier.

1751: the Mureș section ("its entire territory was placed under civil administration"), the civil parts of the Danube section and most of the Tisa section end (table of sections, "1702-1751"); on the Banat side the land returns to civil administration in the Banat of Temeswar.

1751: the Tisa section ("most of its territory was placed under civil administration, while one small area in the south remained under military administration as part of the Šajkaš Battalion") and the Danube section ("one part of its territory was placed under civil administration and another part was joined with…
1751: Maria Theresa introduces civil administration in the north of the Banat while the south stays under military rule: "formed in 1751, out of territories of the Banat of Temeswar".
1762: the Transylvanian Military Frontier is founded, with Romanian regiments at Orlat and Năsăud and Székely regiments at Miercurea Ciuc and Târgu Secuiesc.
1763: "Šajkaš Battalion was formed"; the Banat page says the frontier "included part of Bačka known as Šajkaška".
1783: "The Croatian and Slavonian frontiers were unified under the Zagreb General Command."
1848: eastern Syrmia joins the autonomous Serbian Vojvodina (1848-1849).
1849: the page gives 1848-1849 for the Vojvodina and names no return; bridged to the end of the Vojvodina, confidence 1.
1851: the Transylvanian Military Frontier is abolished.
1871: "The Križevci and Đurđevac regiments joined Croatia-Slavonia."
The Šajkaš Battalion "was abolished in 1873, and its territory was incorporated into Bačka-Bodrog County"; the page gives no month for it (the Banat Frontier fell on 8 August 1873).
8 August 1873: "The Banat Frontier was abolished... and incorporated into Hungary."
1881: the Frontier is "abolished and incorporated into the Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia", decree of 15 July and takeover on 1 August.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1787-1791
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Sistova (1791) ended the war and the Austrian forces withdrew from Serbia; the Frontier's extent did not change.

certainty.note: A line of fortresses and captaincies against the Ottomans; no survey line on the pages opened.

Regimental districts with dated administrative changes (1745, 1751, 1762, 1851, 1871, 1873, 1881); the Ottoman frontier is the treaty line of Karlowitz and Passarowitz, although the pages give no coordinates.
